summary:
The United Kingdom's Equality Act 2010 and its 2025 single-sex-services code do not automatically extend to Bermuda. Local legislation governs, and United Kingdom measures could be applied to Bermuda only by Order in Council.

The House of Assembly voted 22–16 on 14 May 1994 to decriminalise consensual sex between adult men, striking two sections of the Criminal Code. The debate divided the island at the time, with religious leaders split and the Christian Coalition staging marches against the change.

In July 2013 the Senate passed the Human Rights Amendment Act, which outlawed discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation and, in the same instrument, on grounds of age. Same-sex marriage was not permitted at that point.

The Governor gave assent to the Domestic Partnership Act in February 2018. It replaced same-sex marriage with domestic partnerships open to same-sex and opposite-sex couples alike, which made Bermuda the first jurisdiction to revoke marriage equality.
tangentialFactors:
Organised religious hostility toward visible same-sex couples has been publicly demonstrated. In 2018 the AME church and other Bermuda congregations protested a gay cruise calling it incompatible with the word of God and the Christian moral fibre, and in 1994 the Christian Coalition marched against decriminalisation.

Sexual-orientation protection was legislated alongside age as a protected ground in a single 2013 instrument, rather than enacted separately.

The 2018 partnership law applied to opposite-sex couples as well, giving Bermuda a civil-status regime distinct from the marriage frameworks used elsewhere in comparable jurisdictions.
localsOnly:
Residents gained the ability to enter a legally recognised domestic partnership from February 2018, after the Governor's assent to the Domestic Partnership Act 2017.

Consensual sex between adult men has not been a criminal offence in Bermuda since the House of Assembly's 1994 vote, and discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation has been prohibited under the Human Rights Amendment Act since 2013.

Marriage equality, which had been available during 2017, was withdrawn the following year and replaced by domestic partnerships.
outOfScopeNotes:
The source inventory does not address legal gender recognition, changes of name or gender markers on local identity documents, or passport and entry-document rules for trans visitors; the current position on those matters is unresolved here.

Enforcement practice under the 2013 sexual-orientation discrimination protection, and whether hate-crime or aggravated-offence provisions cover anti-trans violence, are not sourced.

Whether same-sex marriage has been restored, challenged or litigated after February 2018 is unresolved in these sources.

The mechanism and practical scope of any Order in Council applying a United Kingdom statute to Bermuda is not specified in the sources.
